name: Baylor Veer N Shoot
subtitle: Baylor Bears · CFB 27
tagline: Spread them wide. Then go over the top.

about.headline: WHO ARE THE BEARS
copy: Art Briles brought the offense from Stephenville and Houston to Waco in 2008, and by 2011 it had turned a program that had not won ten games since 1980 into the most explosive offense in the country. Robert Griffin III won the Heisman, the first in Baylor history, and the Bears went {rec|10-3}.

Griffin threw for {yds|4,293 yards} and 37 touchdowns against six picks, completed 72 percent of his throws, and ran for 699 more. Kendall Wright caught 108 balls for 1,663 yards. Terrance Ganaway ran for 1,547 and 21 scores. They beat a top five Oklahoma on a walk off touchdown to Terrance Williams, the first time Baylor had ever beaten the Sooners.

Then they won the Alamo Bowl 67-56 over Washington, the highest scoring regulation bowl game ever played. They did it with receivers split out to the numbers, option routes that were right against every coverage, and a quarterback who could beat you with his legs or his arm. That is the offense we are building, out of the Auburn playbook in College Football 27.

principles.title: SPREAD THEM WIDE
principles.blurb: Receivers split all the way to the numbers, not to look different, but to make the defense declare before the snap.
principles.detail: Briles put his receivers on the numbers because a defender who has to cover that much grass has to declare before the snap, and every declaration tells the quarterback something. A safety who widens to help on the numbers cannot get back to the middle, so the seams open, and a box that has to send bodies out wide cannot stop the run without help. In the game it works the same way: single high with these wide alignments leaves the seams open for big plays, and two high gives you a light box and lets you attack the middle of the field.

principles.title: THE ROUTE IS ALWAYS RIGHT
principles.blurb: Option routes that decide after the snap. The receiver sees the coverage and finishes with the route that beats it.
principles.detail: Briles did not need a big playbook, because a choice route is three plays in one: the receiver runs his stem, reads what the coverage did, and finishes with the route it cannot cover. It makes the offense much more adaptable, because no matter what the call is, the receivers and the quarterback can move to a look that beats it. In the game it is the answer to a defense we cannot figure out: call the choice, read the same picture the receiver reads, and let the route be right.

principles.title: THE QUARTERBACK IS A WEAPON
principles.blurb: A quarterback who can take off or throw it sixty yards. The defense has to be right about both, and it cannot be.
principles.detail: Griffin was a world class athlete with a real arm, and Briles built the offense around both: the reads and midline made the box account for him, and the shots over the top punished them for it. Every defender pulled down to stop the quarterback run is one fewer over the top, and every safety kept deep for the shot is one fewer in the box, so the defense is wrong before the ball is snapped. In the game it plays exactly like that: the reads take the light box, and when they cheat to stop them, the deep ball is there.

playbook.title: RUN THE AUBURN PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In College Football 27 this whole offense runs out of the AUBURN playbook. All three Wide formations and every call on the sheet live inside it.

jobs: READ THE END ON THE RPO AND KEEP IT WHEN HE CRASHES.
READ THE TACKLE ON MIDLINE AND GO STRAIGHT DOWNHILL.
WATCH ONE SIDE OF THE FIELD ON THE RPOS AND THROW OR RUN.
THROW THE CHOICE ROUTE WHERE THE MIDDLE OF THE FIELD SAYS.
TAKE OFF OUT OF THE ROLLOUT WHEN NOBODY IS THERE.
RUN THE STREAK THAT PULLS THE DEEP DEFENDER.
SWITCH RELEASE AND WHEEL ON PA CHOICE DEEP.
WIN THE DEEP DIG AGAINST MAN.
BLOCK ON THE SWING.
RUN THE OPTION ROUTE: SEAM, POST, DIG OR SIT.
WIN THE SEAM AGAINST SINGLE HIGH.
RUN THE COMEBACK FROM THE SLOT AGAINST MAN.
MAKE THE FIRST MAN MISS ON THE HITCH.
MOTION ACROSS AND PULL THE USER.
RUN THE DEEP CROSS BEHIND THE PLAY FAKE.
RUN THE ANGLE OUT AND BACK UP THE MIDDLE.
LEAD BLOCK ON THE SWING.
TAKE THE GIVE DOWNHILL WHEN THEY SHUT THE EDGE.
RUN THE SWING TO THE PERIMETER.
BE THE FLAT ON EVERY PLAY ACTION.
OPTION ROUTE OUT OF THE BACKFIELD AGAINST MAN.

player.name: ROBERT GRIFFIN III
player.line: The Heisman. A world class athlete who could throw it seventy yards.
player.bio: Came to Baylor from Copperas Cove as a track star who happened to play quarterback, and left as the first Heisman winner in school history. In 2011 he threw for {yds|4,293 yards} and 37 touchdowns against six picks, completed 72 percent, and ran for 699 more. He beat a top five Oklahoma with eight seconds left, won the Davey O'Brien Award, and then went second overall in the draft.
roleFor: The quarterback in this offense makes the whole thing go. He reads one man on the RPOs and on midline and keeps it when that man crashes, he watches one side of the field on the alert plays and throws or runs off what he sees, and on the play action he throws the choice route where the middle of the field tells him: the post if it is open, the dig if it is closed.

The legs are the extra weapon, not the job. When he rolls out on Dash Flood and nobody is there he takes off, and the threat of that is what keeps the box light for everybody else. Deep accuracy, throwing on the run and speed are the three things this role cannot live without.
player.oneLine: Read one man, throw it where the field says, run when it is there.

lineage.name: ROBERT GRIFFIN III
lineage.brought: The fastest player on the field and the arm to go with it. The reason the box was light and the shots were open.

player.name: TERRANCE WILLIAMS
player.line: The outside receiver on the numbers. The Oklahoma game winner.
player.bio: The outside receiver on the 2011 team, and the one who caught the 34 yard touchdown with eight seconds left to beat fifth ranked Oklahoma, the first time Baylor had ever beaten the Sooners. The next season he led the whole country with 1,832 receiving yards and was a unanimous All-American before the Cowboys drafted him.
goodAt: Runs the switch release choice route.
roleFor: The outside receiver in this offense lines up on the numbers and holds the deep defender with the streak on almost every call, which is what opens the seam and the crosser inside of him. On PA Choice Deep he switch releases and wheels up the sideline for the back shoulder ball.

Against man he wins the deep dig on Shock H Option and the corner on Whip Curl Flat. Deep speed, a clean release and ball skills are what the job needs, because most of his throws come with one man on him and nobody else.
player.oneLine: Hold the deep defender, then win the one on one.

lineage.name: TERRANCE WILLIAMS
stats: The walk off touchdown to beat Oklahoma
Led the nation in receiving yards the next year
lineage.brought: The outside receiver on the numbers. The switch release choice route and the streak that runs the deep defender off.

player.name: KENDALL WRIGHT
player.line: The slot star. 108 catches in the Heisman season.
player.bio: The slot receiver who caught everything in 2011: 108 receptions for 1,663 yards and 14 touchdowns, first team All-American, and the third receiver taken in the 2012 draft when the Titans picked him twentieth overall. Quick in and out of his breaks and fast enough to take the seam the distance.
roleFor: The slot receiver is the option route, which is who this offense throws to most of the game. On PA Slot Choice he stems up one notch and turns the curl into a seam against single high, and against two high he becomes the post or the dig. On PA Deep Choice the same route reads the safeties and decides itself.

Against man he runs the comeback from the slot on Shock H Option, which you cannot normally do from there. Release, agility and soft hands, because he is the one the quarterback is looking at first on the essentials.
player.oneLine: The option route the whole offense throws to.

lineage.name: KENDALL WRIGHT
lineage.brought: The slot star. The option route he throws to all game, and the seam against single high.

player.name: TEVIN REESE
player.line: The speed inside. A 4.41 forty and 877 yards as a sophomore.
player.bio: The inside receiver on the 2011 team: 51 catches for 877 yards and seven touchdowns as a sophomore, then 957 yards the next year, then a senior season at 22.8 yards a catch, the second best in Baylor history. Ran a 4.41 at the combine. The one who could take the top off from the inside.
roleFor: The inside slot in this offense is the tight end spot in the game's formations, and he is the one who motions. On MTN TE Angle he goes out like he is blocking the swing and cuts back up the middle. On MTN PA Y Cross he is the shallower cross behind the play fake, and the post when you want to attack deeper.
On Deep Stick and QB Zone he is the man motioned across, the clear out on one and the extra blocker on the other. Speed, hands and a release, because he is the one running past the linebackers.
player.oneLine: The motion man who runs past the linebackers.

lineage.name: TEVIN REESE
lineage.brought: The speed inside. The seam, the deep cross, and the motion that pulls the user.

player.name: TERRANCE GANAWAY
player.line: The downhill back. 1,547 yards and 21 scores, then five in the Alamo Bowl.
player.bio: The senior running back on the 2011 team: 1,547 rushing yards and 21 touchdowns, then 200 yards and five scores in the Alamo Bowl win over Washington that made him the game's MVP. The 89 yard run in the third quarter and the 43 yarder that iced it were both his.
roleFor: The back in this offense gets the give when the end shuts the edge on the read, and when he gets it the box is light because of the splits. On MTN HB Swing he is the auto motion swing with the tight end leading, and that one went ninety nine yards.

On every play action he is the flat, the checkdown that is there when the deep routes are covered, and on Shock H Option he option routes out of the backfield against man. Acceleration, hands and vision in the open field.
player.oneLine: The give, the swing, and the flat on every play fake.

lineage.name: TERRANCE GANAWAY
stats: Alamo Bowl MVP: 200 yards and five scores
lineage.brought: The downhill back. The give on the read, the swing, and the flat on every play action.

pillars.name: Base Spread Offense
pillars.eyebrow: the motion run and what comes off it
pillars.line: Where every game starts. This section is the run game, the motion and the play action that comes off it, so the defense has to stop the base before it gets to worry about anything else. The goal is to get comfortable in the three formations, learn what the motion tells you about the coverage, and build the foundation that the shots and the option routes are going to come off of.

checks: The user starts jumping the motion and the flip
The play action flood comes off the same picture they just chased
They go man to stop it and the option routes break away from everybody

pillars.name: Veer N Shoot Essentials
pillars.line: This is the part of the offense that made Baylor Baylor. A choice route does not run a set path: the receiver reads the coverage after the snap and finishes with the route that beats it, so one call has an answer for every shell they can show you. This section is about learning to read the same picture he reads, so when you cannot figure a defense out you call the choice and let the route be right.

checks: Middle open, the choice route is a post over the top
Middle closed, it is a dig in front of the safety
The wheel and the drag are layered off the same routes

pillars.name: Explosive QB Offense
pillars.line: The quarterback as a weapon, with his legs and his arm. Griffin was as dangerous taking off as he was throwing it sixty yards, and that is what made the defense wrong no matter what it did: load the box and the shot goes over the top, stay deep and he runs straight through the light box. This section is about using both, the designed quarterback runs and the deep shots, so the defense never gets to be right.

checks: The tackle crashes and midline goes straight downhill

You are out of the pocket with the back in front of you and an open edge

home.pitch: Receivers split to the numbers, option routes that are right against every coverage, and a quarterback who is a weapon with his legs and his arm. All of it out of the Auburn playbook.

book.note: every formation and every call on the sheet lives inside it

plays.name: MTN RPO Read Flat

reads.label: Read the End
reads.text: Read the end man on the line of scrimmage, the one with the R over his head. If he crashes down on the back, keep it. If he shuts down the edge at the snap, hand it off and let the back get downhill away from the flow.

reads.label: The Flip to the Motion Man
reads.text: This is where it turns into a triple option. You pulled it, the end is coming at you, and the motion man is coming across the formation right in front of you. Flip it out to him with blockers in front.

reads.label: Keep It
reads.text: Pulling it does not mean you have to throw it. Once the user has seen the flip a few times he leaves the box to cover it. Now the receivers climb to the second level and you keep it and run into a big pocket.

reads.label: The Give
reads.text: If at the snap they shut down the edge, hand it off. The blocking goes away from the motion and the whole flow of the play, and the back hits the edge on the other side.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field, so the motion comes across to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: The play you can build the whole offense around. Read the end, and then the flip and the keep are there once the user starts reacting to it. MTN PA Y Cross is the exact same motion, so this is what earns the shot.

plays.name: MTN PA Y Cross

reads.label: The Corner Over the Flat
reads.text: Same motion and the same look as MTN RPO Read Flat, but it is play action and a flood to the wide side. High low the flat defender. If he stays at ten yards or bites down, throw the corner as he breaks up along the sideline.

reads.label: The Tight End Cross
reads.text: The shallower cross comes across the middle behind the play fake. Against man he is running away from his defender. Against zone, if the corner is taken away, come inside to him.

reads.label: The Tight End on a Post
reads.text: Hot route the tight end to a post if you want to attack deeper. Now both vertical routes are open when the flat stays shallow, and you can put it up over the top of the linebacker.

reads.label: The Motion Man in the Flat
reads.text: Once he motions across, if everybody plays back on the corner and the cross, drop it down to him in the flat. Fourth and one, easy pickup.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field, so the motion comes across the same way
Optional: tight end on a post to attack deeper
plays.whenToUse: Call it once MTN RPO Read Flat has them jumping the motion. The picture is identical and the flood hits the flat defender they just left. Zone or man.

plays.name: RPO Alert QB Power Wk

reads.label: Watch the Trips Side
reads.text: Keep it simple. Watch the linebackers and the safety on the trips side of the field. If they bite down or bite inside, we throw the slant every time.

reads.label: The Inside Slant
reads.text: The only route you ever need to throw. It is a skinny post more than a slant, and when those defenders come down there is a huge pocket right behind them. Drop it in and it is gone.

reads.label: Hold It and Run
reads.text: If they stay over the receiver, this is QB power with the blocking built in. Hold the ball, let the blocks set up, get downhill with your athletic quarterback for ten or fifteen.

reads.label: Motion the H-Back Over
reads.text: The H-back lines up opposite the trips. Sometimes the end gets too far up the field, so motion the H-back over and he blocks the end while the guard leads you through the hole.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Optional: solo receiver on a slant for a second throw
Optional: motion the H-back across to block the end
plays.whenToUse: One of the best RPOs in the game. One read, one throw, and a quarterback power run when the throw is not there. Call it on early downs all game.

plays.name: Shock H Option

reads.label: The Tight End Option Route
reads.text: The go to route against man. He gets even with his defender, breaks off by three or four yards to the outside, and option routes get separation nobody talks about. Drop it in, rack catch, easy first down.

reads.label: The In-Breaker
reads.text: The outside receiver comes in on the shallow cross into the same field of vision. If the tight end is covered, the in cut is breaking right in behind it. That one went to the one yard line.

reads.label: The Back on the Option
reads.text: The running back option routes too: he sits down against zone, and against man he breaks outside or runs a Texas route into the middle. Two to three yards of separation every time.

reads.label: The Comeback From the Slot
reads.text: You cannot usually put a comeback on a slot receiver, but in these wide sets you can. He goes up the field, comes back to the football, and comebacks are money against man this year.

reads.label: The Backside Dig
reads.text: The deep dig from the solo receiver is the last look. It is deep enough that you have time to work through everything else first.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the trips side on a shallow cross (or a slant off the hash)
Slot receiver on a comeback
If they are not blitzing, send the back and the tight end out
plays.whenToUse: The man beating play. Five routes that all beat man, and the option routes sit down against zone so it is never wasted. When they spam man, this is the call.

plays.name: PA Choice Deep

reads.label: Middle Open or Closed
reads.text: The true veer and shoot essential. The outside receiver switch releases inside and reads the middle of the field: is there a safety in the middle, are the safeties outside, or is nobody deep? He can hook, dig or post, and most of the time it is the dig or the post.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: No deep safeties at the snap, he turns it into a post. Great separation off the line, nobody over the top, and you bomb it. That one scored on fourth and three.

reads.label: The Dig
reads.text: Safeties high, or a single high safety in the middle, he runs the dig underneath instead of running into them. If the linebackers stay shallow, throw it in front of the safety. Against man with a safety over the top it is the dig again.

reads.label: The Wheel, Back Shoulder
reads.text: The slot receiver switch releases outside, and his option route almost never options: he wheels up the sideline. The motioned tight end runs the deep defenders off, and once the wheel clears the flat defender you throw the back shoulder ball along the sideline. Cover 3 or Cover 2.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: A layered concept in the middle: when the deeper routes are taken away, the drag comes across underneath.

reads.label: The Cover 3 Bomb
reads.text: Against Cover 3 the middle safety gets pulled down by the dig, the backside deep third gets caught between two routes, and you can throw it up over the top of everybody. One play touchdowns in practice mode.

adjustments: Tight end to the wide side of the field
Tight end on a streak, then motion him across
Solo receiver on a drag
plays.whenToUse: The play that teaches how the option routes work. Post if the middle is open, dig if it is closed, and the wheel and the drag layered off it. Call it the first time you want a shot off play action.

plays.name: PA Deep Choice

reads.label: The Tight End Cross
reads.text: Play action right in the middle of the field pulls the linebackers down, the streak pulls the deep defender back, and the tight end cross comes across the field for a big gain. Not the option part, just a really good route.

reads.label: The Slot Option Against Two High
reads.text: Two high safeties and most of the time he runs across the field on the dig instead of sitting. Cover 2, match, either one. Throw him the dig first.

reads.label: The Post Behind the Dig
reads.text: If the linebackers stay shallow and take the dig away, wait for the post coming in behind him from the outside. Dig first, then the post in the pocket behind it. Cover 2 with the safeties split, that post goes right down the middle.

reads.label: The Sit Against Single High
reads.text: Single high and he sits down in the zone. If they are in a hard flat look and the flat defender stays shallow, drop it in behind him as he sits.

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: If the flat defender stays back when he sits, the running back is in the flat right underneath. Four options on one play.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Solo receiver on a streak
Outside receiver on the wide side on a post
plays.whenToUse: The second essential, the same option route out of trips. The cross, the dig, the post and the sit all come off one play fake, so there is an answer for every shell.

plays.name: Midline Read Option

reads.label: Read the Tackle
reads.text: Midline changes the picture. Defenses are used to reading the end and scraping over it. Here you let the defensive tackle come up the field and read him instead.

reads.label: Straight Downhill
reads.text: When he crashes, keep it. There is no looping around the edge: the end gets kicked out, the tackle takes himself out of it, and you put your foot in the ground and go straight downhill with no wasted movement.

reads.label: The Give
reads.text: If the tackle stops his feet, or he is unblocked and keeping it is not a good look, or you see a linebacker coming from the second level, hand it off and the back gets downhill for twelve.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: Love it inside the five and on two point tries for the same reason. You are not trying to get to the edge, you are downhill right away.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The quarterback run that goes straight downhill instead of around the edge. Red zone, goal line, two point conversions, and any time they have started scraping to the edge on the read.

plays.name: Deep Stick

reads.label: The Deep Stick
reads.text: Look at the route the play is named after first. A stick sits down against zone and breaks to the sideline against man, and this one runs to seven or eight yards instead of four. Read the flat defender: if he bites down on the H-back, the stick sits in the soft spot behind him.

reads.label: The H-Back to the Flat
reads.text: The H-back comes across the formation to the flat on the stick side. If the flat defender sinks under the stick, drop it down to him. First down.

reads.label: The Dig
reads.text: Two vertical routes work behind those two: the dig comes into the middle from the backside. If the linebackers all slide to the stick side, he replaces the middle of the field.

reads.label: The Post Behind the Backers
reads.text: The motioned man on the streak is the clear out. He pulls the deep defender back, and the post from the trips side comes in behind the linebackers.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field
Middle receiver on the trips side on a streak, then motion him across to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Shallow, deep and man, all on one call. Read the flat defender for the stick and the H-back, and the dig and the post are there when you have time. The motion is the same one QB Zone uses.

plays.name: Dash Flood

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: A built in rollout that gets your athletic quarterback out on the perimeter. Your eyes are already there, so if they come up field to take the quarterback and the flat defender plays back, drop it to the back running in front of you and let him make a man miss.

reads.label: The Deep Out
reads.text: If the flat defender plays shallower, the deep out is coming in behind him. Throw it up over his head along the sideline. Against man he gets great separation as he breaks.

reads.label: The Backside Shallow Cross
reads.text: Against man there are two good routes: the out, and the shallow cross coming across the middle from the backside. Get out of the pocket, see man, hit whichever one has separation.

reads.label: Take Off
reads.text: You are already out of the pocket. If nobody is there and there is an open edge, use the legs and take whatever is there.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The rollout that lets the quarterback be a runner and a passer on the same snap. Third down, red zone, and any time you want to get him out in space.

plays.name: Bash

reads.label: Treat It as a QB Run
reads.text: One of the most underused quarterback runs in the game. You are reading the end, but most of the time you are just keeping it: fake the handoff and go.

reads.label: Run Away From the Play Side
reads.text: The back goes play side and the quarterback runs the other way. The blocking sets up so well that the read player never really affects your ability to run it, and you do not have to worry about read option conservative.

reads.label: When to Give It
reads.text: It is more feel than a locked in key. If at the snap the defense crashes down hard and there is an open lane for the back, hand it off and let him take it downhill.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
plays.whenToUse: A quarterback run that works no matter how they set up their read option defense. Keep it almost every time, and give it when they crash.

plays.name: MTN TE Angle

reads.label: Pull the User With the Swing
reads.text: It looks identical to MTN HB Swing before the snap: same trips, same auto motion, same swing. Run the swing a few times first so the user jumps down into the box.

reads.label: The Seam
reads.text: The option route in the seam. Single high safety, he keeps going down the seam. In these wide sets the seam gets ridiculously open: the user is out on the swing, the flat is pulled wide, and it is a walk in touchdown against Cover 3.

reads.label: The Tight End Angle Against Two High
reads.text: Split safeties and the option route becomes a post. The tight end goes out like he is blocking the swing, then cuts back up the middle behind the user who widened for it. Third and eleven, drop it in.

reads.label: The Swing Checkdown
reads.text: Everybody dropping under the vertical routes, throw the swing in the flat for six or seven.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The constraint off MTN HB Swing. Once they are jumping the swing, the seam and the tight end angle are open behind them.

plays.name: PA Slot Choice

reads.label: The Seam Before He Sits
reads.text: Against a single high safety the slot option runs a curl, but stem him up one notch and you can throw it as a seam ball before he sits down. As soon as the play fake finishes and he is through the jam, let it go. Wait too long and he sits.

reads.label: The Post Against Two High
reads.text: Two high safeties and he runs the post or the dig. Against Cover 4 it is one on one with no help over the top. Against Cover 2 he splits the safeties, and if there is no deep middle dropper he is wide open.

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: Always the option route first, but the deep crosser is coming across the field behind the streak. Man with separation, or zone in behind the flat defender, fire it in.

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: After the play fake the back is in the flat. Third and nine, everyone dropping back, drop it down.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Both outside receivers on streaks
Slot receiver on the option route: hold L1 and stem it up one notch
plays.whenToUse: A classic veer and shoot play. The slot option is who you throw to most of the game, and stemming him up one notch is what turns the curl into a seam.

plays.name: MTN HB Swing

reads.label: Get It to the Edge
reads.text: No adjustments. Snap it and it is an auto motion swing pass. Three blockers on two defenders plus the ball carrier, so it is really a four on two on the perimeter. That one went ninety nine yards.

reads.label: The Tight End Leads
reads.text: What makes this swing different: instead of holding the edge the tight end comes out on the swing and becomes a lead blocker. He pins everybody in and you walk into the end zone.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: When they overplay the swing to the outside, the backside slant comes into the middle. Drop it in and you are inside the five.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: One of the best swing passes in the game this year because of the tight end wrinkle. A blitz beater and a way to get the ball on the perimeter when they pack the inside.

plays.name: All Go

reads.label: The Seam Against Single High
reads.text: A quick snap play, no adjustments. Single high safety and it is one of the easiest throws in the game out of these wide splits: the streak holds the deep third outside, the deep cross pulls the hook inside, and the seam is wide open because the safety is starting so far away.

reads.label: The Deep Cross
reads.text: Two high, or the seam taken away, come inside to the deep cross. Throw it early if there is no hook linebacker in the middle, or wait until he gets behind the flat defender along the sideline.

reads.label: The Option Route Checkdown
reads.text: The H-back option is the checkdown. He sits down against zone and breaks to the sideline against man, and that route is one of the best in the game for easy separation underneath.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The concept that shows why the wide splits work. Get to the line, call it, and read one spot, two spot, checkdown.

plays.name: Whip Curl Flat

reads.label: The Corner Over the Flat
reads.text: A flood with three unique routes: an outside release corner, a whip, and the H-back option. Read the flat defender. He stops at ten, the corner gets to twenty, and you throw it on the back pylon over his head.

reads.label: The Whip
reads.text: If the flat defender drops deep under the corner, the whip is underneath him. This is not the stock whip and it gets better separation.

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: If everybody leaves the middle to help on the corner, the backside crosser replaces it. High low the flat, then the crosser in the middle.

reads.label: Against Man
reads.text: Put the solo receiver on a shallow cross instead of the streak and you have five man beaters on the field: the corner, the whip, the option, the deep cross and the shallow.

reads.label: The H-Back Option
reads.text: Sits down against zone as the checkdown, breaks to the sideline against man.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Zone setup: solo receiver on a streak
Man setup: solo receiver on a shallow cross (or a slant off the hash)
plays.whenToUse: A flood with a whip and an option route built in, so the same call beats zone and man. Third down money.

plays.name: RPO Alert QB Blast

reads.label: Watch the Trips Side
reads.text: A QB blast with an RPO built in. Read one side of the field: the trips side. At the snap, what are those defenders doing?

reads.label: The Hitch
reads.text: The linebacker bites down, the hitch is wide open right behind him. The timing on it is perfect. Rack, catch and go.

reads.label: The Quick Out
reads.text: They are all inside and nobody jumps out on the out route, throw it to the sideline.

reads.label: Keep It
reads.text: They stay out on the hitch and the out, hold it and run. The H-back leads through the hole with the whole line in front of you.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Middle receiver on the wide side on an out route
plays.whenToUse: The RPO with the most success this year. Two quick throws and a quarterback run, all off watching one side of the field.

plays.name: QB Zone

reads.label: Bring the Slot Over
reads.text: Trips to the short side, then motion the middle slot across the formation. It is the same motion as Deep Stick, so it disguises which one is coming, and it buys an extra blocker on the side you are running to.

reads.label: Follow the H-Back Through the Hole
reads.text: The tight end and the H-back lead through the hole and the receiver you brought over blocks the safety who would otherwise come down right away. Get up the field for fifteen.

reads.label: Get Downhill
reads.text: A quick hitter. No reading, no bouncing, just downhill with your athletic quarterback. Bring him over in the red zone and walk in.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field
Middle slot receiver motioned across the formation
plays.whenToUse: The quick hitting quarterback run with an extra blocker. Same motion as Deep Stick, so run both and they never know which is coming.

plays.name: PA Post Curls

reads.label: The Deep Post
reads.text: The tight end on the streak motions across and pulls everybody back. The play fake pulls the linebackers and the user down because you run the ball so much in this offense. The post comes into a massive hole in the middle. Cover 2, Cover 3, match, the linebackers never get deep enough.

reads.label: The Hitch to the Wide Side
reads.text: Hitches on both sides. Look to the wide side, because the back releases that way and the hitch sits down right in front of him.

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: If everybody plays back under the hitches and the post, throw it to the back and let him make plays in the open field.

reads.label: The Block and Release
reads.text: The tight end blocks for a second, sees if anybody is coming free, then releases. Those routes are good because every defender has dropped by the time he gets out, and there is a lot of room.

adjustments: Tight end to the short side of the field
Tight end on a streak, then motion him across
plays.whenToUse: The play action shot over the middle. The user is the only one who can take the post away, and the hitches and the back are there when he does.
